There are a couple of holes in the module_utils builder redirection stuff for subpackages, esp when the parent package doesn't exist. I've got a hacky fix that works in this case (missing package), but fixing it properly needs a bit of refactoring in the recursive module_util finder (to avoid splattering a bunch of copypasta in several places to handle both "real" and missing pkg init code). I'm on PTO all next week, but this will be high priority for the following week.

A part of the problem seems also to be that ansible-base's ansible_builtin_runtime.yml `plugin_routing.module_utils` seems to have been created with the idea of flatmapping in mind, since no subdirectories are mentioned (except in the examples @nitzmahone added in the routing PR). For example, in pre-ansible-base, there were 10 files called `common.py`: `podman/common.py`, `azure_rm_common.py`, `k8s/common.py`, `remote_management/lxca/common.py`, `docker/common.py`, `network/fortianalyzer/common.py`, `network/fortimanager/common.py`, `network/f5/common.py`, `network/ingate/common.py`, `network/ftd/common.py`. In `plugin_routing.module_utils`, there's precisely one `common` entry, and that points to where *one* of these files went.

Just had a similar error where a vendored version of `ldap_attrs` (added after stable-2.9 was branched) was trying to import `ansible.module_utils.ldap`, which is redirected to `ansible_collections.community.general.plugins.module_utils.ldap`:
```
[...]
  File "/tmp/ansible_ldap_attrs_payload_vosvf7qm/ansible_ldap_attrs_payload.zip/ansible/modules/ldap_attrs.py", line 176, in <module>
  File "/tmp/ansible_ldap_attrs_payload_vosvf7qm/ansible_ldap_attrs_payload.zip/ansible/module_utils/ldap.py", line 3, in <module>
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'community'
```
I haven't looked at the generated payload, but I suspect that either the `ansible/module_utils/ldap.py` file is wrongly created, or the real module_utils from community.general it tries to import wasn't packaged.
